officialTitle: Lobar or Sublobar Resection for Peripheral Stage IA Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: a total of 697 patients were assigned to undergo sublobar resection (340 patients) or lobar resection (357 patients)
design.notes: Non-inferiority design; randomisation after intraoperative confirmation of node-negative disease.

clinicalQuestion: Is sublobar resection non-inferior to lobectomy for disease-free survival in small peripheral node-negative NSCLC?

pico.population: Small peripheral clinically node-negative NSCLC with intraoperatively confirmed node-negative hilar and mediastinal disease
pico.outcomes: Primary: DFS (non-inferiority). Secondary: OS, recurrence, pulmonary function

publications.title: Lobar or Sublobar Resection for Peripheral Stage IA Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: After a median follow-up of 7 years, sublobar resection was noninferior to lobar resection for disease-free survival (hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death, 1.01; 90% confidence interval [CI], 0.83 to 1.24).
The 5-year disease-free survival was 63.6% (95% CI, 57.9 to 68.8) after sublobar resection and 64.1% (95% CI, 58.5 to 69.0) after lobar resection.
In addition, overall survival after sublobar resection was similar to that after lobar resection (hazard ratio for death, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.72 to 1.26).
The 5-year overall survival was 80.3% (95% CI, 75.5 to 84.3) after sublobar resection and 78.9% (95% CI, 74.1 to 82.9) after lobar resection.

strengths: Multicentre randomised non-inferiority trial with long follow-up
Randomisation after intraoperative nodal confirmation reduces stage misclassification
limitations: Sublobar arm included both wedge resection and segmentectomy
Non-inferiority margin assessed with a 90% CI
Applies only to small peripheral node-negative tumours

clinicalImplications.text: Together with JCOG0802, supports sublobar resection as an acceptable alternative to lobectomy for small peripheral node-negative NSCLC when nodal status is confirmed intraoperatively.

tumourBoardPearl.text: The key eligibility step is intraoperative confirmation of node-negative hilar and mediastinal nodes before committing to sublobar resection.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 36780674. Primary DFS HR reported with a 90% CI (ciLevel 90).
